method.label: Count odd and even position patterns

annotationRationale: Addition modulo 2 determines which row and column patterns have odd sums. Classical probability gives the ratio of favorable to equally likely parity patterns. Combinations and the multiplication principle support the counting, while odd/even recognition identifies the five odd entries.
sourceMethod: Followed the official parity-pattern count, adding explicit parity-addition, converse, uniqueness, and equal-likelihood justifications.

review.mathCheck: Independently, each row must contain one or three odd numbers, forcing counts (3,1,1); likewise for columns. The unique all-odd row and column occupy five cells, determining all odd positions. Their 9 possible unions all work. Each of the 126 choices of four even positions has 5!4! arrangements, so the probability is 9/126 = 1/14, choice B. The candidate covers necessity, sufficiency, and duplicate counting.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, originally worded adaptation of official solution 20 on pages 11–12: identify the all-odd row and column, count 9 favorable patterns, and divide by C(9,4). The added overlap, converse, uniqueness, and equal-likelihood explanations make the method reconstructible at AMC 10 level.
review.annotationCheck: The assessed probability and additive-parity skills are central. Combinations, multiplication counting, and odd/even recognition appropriately support them. No material concept omission or incorrect direct selection.
